mainTopic: How a נגזל, a buyer and a creditor collect the קרן, פירות and שבח, and שמואל's rules on שבח for a buyer from a robber and for a creditor.
overview: The amud opens by finishing רבה בר רב הונא's explanation of the ברייתא about a stolen field: thugs seized it, so the נגזל collects the קרן from sold property and the פירות only from free property. The גמרא shows that רבא and רבה בר רב הונא each read the phrase 'הרי היא יוצאה מתחת ידו' differently. רב אשי offers a third reading: the buyer collects the קרן and the נגזל collects the פירות. The גמרא then asks how a מלוה על פה can be collected from liened property. It answers that the robber stood trial for the קרן before he sold his land. Next the גמרא questions שמואל's view that a לוקח מגזלן gets no שבח. רב יוסף answers in two versions: the robber owns land, or a קנין was made, and a sale is different from a loan like סאה בסאה. The גמרא then returns to שמואל's rule that a בעל חוב collects the שבח. רבא proves it from the wording of a sale document and accepts that a gift is stronger than a sale in this respect. Finally, two ברייתות are brought. The second one is defended for שמואל in two ways, and the second defense continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבה בר רב הונא: thugs took the field from the robber
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב הונא finishes his explanation of the ברייתא. The case is one where thugs seized the field from the robber. The נגזל collects the קרן from sold, liened property, and the פירות only from free, unsold property.
steps.simpleTranslation: [The case is] where thugs took the field away. When the victim comes to collect the principal, he collects from liened property. When the victim comes to collect for the produce, he collects only from free property.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing רבה בר רב הונא's explanation of the ברייתא. In his case, thugs grabbed the stolen field from the robber.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the field is gone, the robber owes its value (the קרן) and the value of the produce (the פירות). The ברייתא says the קרן can be collected even from property the robber already sold (נכסים משועבדים), but the פירות only from property he still owns (נכסים בני חורין).

keyTerms.meaning: Violent thugs or strongmen who seize land by force
The robbery victim
The principal; here, the value of the field itself
Liened property: land the debtor already sold to others, which a creditor can sometimes take from the buyers
Free property: land the debtor still owns and has not sold

steps.confusionAlert: This line begins in the middle of a sentence. The words 'for example, where...' belong to רבה בר רב הונא, whose explanation started just before this point.

phrases.english: [for example,] where thugs took it [the field] away,
when the robbery victim comes to collect the principal –
he collects from liened property;
when the robbery victim comes to collect for the produce –
he collects from free (unsold) property.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁנְּטָלוּהָ מַסִּיקִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבה בר רב הונא's explanation of the ברייתא, which is an alternative to רבא's explanation given just before.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ברייתא is talking about a field that thugs seized from the robber. The קרן is collected from נכסים משועבדים and the פירות from נכסים בני חורין.

steps.title: Why רבא did not explain it like רבה בר רב הונא
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects the thugs explanation. The wording 'it goes out from under his hand' means the field was taken away through a court ruling, not seized by thugs.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא did not explain it like רבה בר רב הונא, because 'it goes out from under his hand' implies [it was taken] by law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבא did not accept רבה בר רב הונא's explanation. The answer is based on a word in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says the field 'goes out from under his hand'. רבא reads this as a legal removal by a court. A field grabbed by thugs was not taken 'by law', so רבה בר רב הונא's case does not fit the wording.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It goes out from under his hand': the ברייתא's phrase for the field being taken away from its holder
By law, through a court ruling
It implies, it suggests

phrases.english: Rava did not say [his explanation]
like Rabba bar Rav Huna,
[because the phrase] 'it goes out from under his hand' –
implies [it was taken away] by law.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא לָא אָמַר כְּרַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why רבא would not accept the case given in step 1.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבה בר רב הונא's case of a field seized by thugs.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The phrase 'יוצאה מתחת ידו' points to a court taking the field away, not thugs.

steps.title: Why רבה בר רב הונא did not explain it like רבא
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב הונא rejects רבא's explanation. The wording 'it goes out from under his hand' means the field goes back intact, so it could not be a damaged field.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבה בר רב הונא did not explain it like רבא, because 'it goes out from under his hand' implies [it goes out] intact.
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא gives the other side: why רבה בר רב הונא did not accept רבא's explanation, which spoke of a damaged field.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה בר רב הונא reads the same phrase differently: the field 'goes out' whole and unchanged. That does not fit רבא's case of a field that was damaged. So the two disagree only about what this one phrase implies.

keyTerms.meaning: In its original, intact form; unchanged

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא לָא אָמַר
phrases.english: And Rabba bar Rav Huna did not say [his explanation]
like Rava,
[because the phrase] 'it goes out from under his hand' –
implies [it goes out] intact.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא לָא אָמַר כְּרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The mirror image of step 2: now רבה בר רב הונא's reason for rejecting רבא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבא's explanation involving a damaged field.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The phrase 'יוצאה מתחת ידו' implies the field goes out intact, not damaged.
steps.whatToRemember: Both רבא and רבה בר רב הונא build on the same phrase, 'הרי היא יוצאה מתחת ידו'. רבא hears 'by law', and רבה בר רב הונא hears 'intact'.

steps.title: רב אשי: the ברייתא speaks of two different people
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says the ברייתא teaches לצדדין, about two different claimants. The robber ate the produce and sold the field. The לוקח collects the קרן (his purchase price) from נכסים משועבדים, while the נגזל collects for the פירות only from נכסים בני חורין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: the ברייתא teaches about separate sides. For example, someone stole a field full of produce from another, ate the produce and sold the field. When the buyer comes to collect the principal, he collects from liened property. When the victim comes to collect for the produce, he collects from free property.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי offers a brand-new, third way to read the ברייתא. He says its two rulings are about two different people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא and רבה בר רב הונא had the נגזל collecting both the קרן and the פירות. רב אשי says the קרן is collected by the buyer, who paid for the field and lost it when the real owner took it back. The פירות are collected by the נגזל, whose produce the robber ate.

keyTerms.meaning: It teaches 'to the sides': the cases in the text refer to different people or situations
The buyer who purchased the field from the robber

steps.confusionAlert: In רב אשי's reading, the one collecting the קרן is the לוקח (buyer), not the נגזל. Only the פירות go to the נגזל.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
it teaches [its rulings] about separate sides,
for example, where someone stole a field from his fellow
full of produce,
and he ate the produce
and sold the field;
when the buyer comes to collect the principal –
he collects from liened property.
When the robbery victim comes to collect for the produce –
he collects from free property.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר לִצְדָדִין קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third explanation of the ברייתא that does not follow either רבא or רבה בר רב הונא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The buyer collects the קרן from נכסים משועבדים; the נגזל collects for the פירות from נכסים בני חורין.

steps.title: Challenge: a robber's debt is only an oral loan
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges both רבא and רבה בר רב הונא. The robber's debt to the נגזל is only a מלוה על פה, a debt without a document, and such a debt cannot be collected from נכסים משועבדים. So how can the נגזל collect the קרן from liened property?
steps.simpleTranslation: According to both רבא and רבה בר רב הונא, it is an oral loan, and an oral loan cannot be collected from liened property!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now raises a difficulty against the explanations of both רבא and רבה בר רב הונא. The next step answers it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In both of their explanations, the נגזל collects the קרן from sold property. But the robber never signed a document for the נגזל, so his debt is like a מלוה על פה, which cannot be collected from נכסים משועבדים. רב אשי is not included in the challenge, because in his reading the קרן is collected by the buyer, who has a written sale document from the robber, so his claim is not a מלוה על פה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Whether according to... or according to...': the challenge works against both opinions
An oral loan: a debt with no written document

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a key rule of debt collection: a creditor may take liened property from buyers only when the debt is backed by a document. It also explains why רב אשי's reading avoids the problem.

phrases.english: Whether according to Rava
or according to Rabba bar Rav Huna,
it is an oral loan,
phrases.notes: He means the robber's debt to the victim, since nothing about it was ever written down.

phrases.english: and an oral loan
cannot be collected from liened property!

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּין לְרָבָא בֵּין לְרַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא מִלְוָה עַל פֶּה הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the explanations of רבא and רבה בר רב הונא and challenges them both.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanations of רבא and רבה בר רב הונא, in which the נגזל collects the קרן from נכסים משועבדים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The robber's debt to the נגזל has no document, so it is a מלוה על פה. A מלוה על פה cannot be collected from liened property. So the נגזל should not be able to collect the קרן from נכסים משועבדים.

steps.title: The robber stood trial before he sold his property
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the question from step 5: the case is where the robber first stood trial and only afterward sold his property, so that property is now נכסים משועבדים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here we are dealing with a case where the robber stood trial and afterward sold [his property].
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question of how the נגזל can collect the קרן from liened property. It explains that the robber was taken to בית דין first, and only after that did he sell his land to others.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A normal מלוה על פה cannot be collected from נכסים משועבדים, because buyers had no way to know about it. But once the robber stood trial, his debt became publicly known, so it is treated like a written debt. Buyers who bought from him after that should have been careful.

keyTerms.meaning: Here, what are we dealing with? (a phrase that limits the case to a specific situation)
He stood trial in בית דין
And afterward he sold

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a debt with no document can still be collected from liened property once a court case has made it publicly known.

phrases.english: Here, what are we dealing with?
When he stood trial, and afterward sold.
phrases.notes: Because he was already taken to court, his debt was known, so it works like a debt written in a document.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 5 (a מלוה על פה cannot be collected from נכסים משועבדים).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The robber's debt is a simple מלוה על פה, which cannot be collected from liened property.
steps.terutzMaskana: He stood trial before selling, so the debt was publicly known and can be collected from liened property.

steps.title: Then the produce should be collected from liened property too
steps.stepSummary: If standing trial makes the debt collectible from liened property, the פירות should also be collectible from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the produce too should be collected from liened property!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave. If the trial made the debt known, why does the ברייתא say the פירות are collected only from free property?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא makes a difference between the קרן (liened property) and the פירות (free property only). If the trial is what makes the debt collectible from liened property, that reason should cover the פירות as well, so the difference disappears.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
Also, too

phrases.english: If so, the produce too!
phrases.notes: He means: the payment for the produce should also be collected from liened property.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, פֵּירוֹת נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the robber stood trial before selling.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Standing trial should make all of the robber's debt collectible from liened property, including the פירות, but the ברייתא says the פירות come only from free property.

steps.title: He stood trial only for the principal
steps.stepSummary: The robber stood trial for the קרן but not yet for the פירות.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he stood trial for the principal, but did not stand trial for the produce.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the trial was only about the field itself (the קרן). The פירות were never brought to court, so that part of the debt stayed a plain unknown debt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the part of the debt that was judged becomes publicly known. The קרן was judged, so it can come from liened property. The פירות were not judged, so they are still a מלוה על פה and come only from free property.

keyTerms.meaning: For the principal (the field itself)
For the produce

phrases.english: When he stood trial for the principal,
but did not stand trial for the produce.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּשֶׁעָמַד בַּדִּין עַל הַקֶּרֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 7.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The trial covered everything, so the פירות should also come from liened property.
steps.terutzMaskana: The trial covered only the קרן, so only the קרן comes from liened property.

steps.title: Why does the ברייתא state it as a flat rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא states the rule in general terms, when it really depends on which part he stood trial for.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why does it state it without any condition?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording of the ברייתא. If the real difference is what he was judged for, why does the ברייתא speak simply about 'קרן' and 'פירות'?
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to step 8, the real line is between a debt that was judged and a debt that was not. But the ברייתא presents it as if קרן and פירות always have different rules. The ברייתא should have said it depends on the trial.

keyTerms.meaning: And why is it stated as a fixed rule?

phrases.english: And why is it stated without any condition?
phrases.notes: Literally 'what is decided?' He means: why does the ברייתא give a flat rule when it really depends on the situation?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי פַּסְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 8 based on the ברייתא's wording.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that he stood trial only for the קרן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the rule depends on what was judged, the ברייתא should not split the rule simply between קרן and פירות.

steps.title: People usually claim the principal first
steps.stepSummary: Usually a person sues for the קרן first, so the ברייתא describes the normal situation.
steps.simpleTranslation: The usual way of things is that when a person makes a claim, he claims the principal first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is describing what normally happens. A person who sues usually asks for the main thing, the field, before asking for the produce.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since people normally go to court for the קרן first, the usual situation is that the קרן was judged and the פירות were not yet judged. So the ברייתא could state the rule simply as 'קרן from liened property, פירות from free property.'

keyTerms.meaning: The usual way of things
He made a claim in court
First

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא's split between קרן and פירות is explained as: the robber stood trial for the קרן before he sold, so it was publicly known; the פירות were not yet judged. People normally sue for the קרן first.

phrases.english: The usual way of things is,
when a person makes a claim,
he claims the principal first.

steps.triggerLanguage: סְתָמָא דְמִילְּתָא כִּי תָּבַע אִינִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 9 and closes this line of questioning.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining that the ברייתא describes the usual case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא should have stated a condition instead of a flat rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since people normally claim the קרן first, the usual case fits the flat rule.

steps.title: Does שמואל really deny the buyer the enhancement?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether שמואל holds that a buyer from a robber gets no שבח, since שמואל told רב חיננא בר שילת to write 'שופרא שבחא ופירי' in documents.
steps.simpleTranslation: And does שמואל hold that one who buys from a robber does not get the enhancement? But שמואל said to רב חיננא בר שילת: Consult, and write 'superior land, enhancement, and produce.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new question about שמואל's earlier statement that a buyer from a robber does not get paid for the שבח. It shows that שמואל himself told a writer of documents to include שבח in the document.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, שמואל's view was quoted that a לוקח מגזלן has no claim for שבח. But שמואל instructed רב חיננא בר שילת to write in a sale document that the seller guarantees better land, the שבח, and the פירות. That suggests a buyer does get the שבח, which seems to contradict שמואל's earlier view.

keyTerms.meaning: One who buys from a robber
The enhancement, the increase in the field's value
Consult (with the people involved)
The best quality (land)

steps.whyThisMatters: This opens a new discussion about whether a buyer can claim the שבח back from the seller when the field is taken from him.

phrases.english: And does שמואל hold
that one who buys from a robber does not have the enhancement?
phrases.notes: This goes back to שמואל's earlier statement that such a buyer gets back his money but not the שבח.

phrases.english: But didn't שמואל say
to רב חיננא בר שילת:
Consult, and write
'the best land, the enhancement, and the produce.'
phrases.notes: These words go in a sale document: if the field is taken away, the seller pays for all of these.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְסָבַר שְׁמוּאֵל לוֹקֵחַ מִגַּזְלָן לֵית לֵיהּ שְׁבָחָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, questioning שמואל's earlier statement about a לוקח מגזלן.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's view that a לוקח מגזלן has no claim for שבח.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל himself told רב חיננא בר שילת to write the שבח into sale documents, which suggests a buyer does get the שבח.

steps.title: The document wording must refer to a buyer from a robber
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that 'שופרא שבחא ופירי' cannot refer to a creditor taking the land, because a בעל חוב does not collect פירות. So it must refer to a buyer from a גזלן, and that contradicts שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which case is this document wording about? If it is about a creditor, does a creditor get produce? But שמואל said a creditor collects the improvement: the improvement yes, the produce no. So it must be about someone who bought from a robber!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the question from Step 11. It proves that the document wording must be talking about a buyer from a גזלן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The document wording promises the buyer the field's improvement and its produce. A בעל חוב never takes produce, according to שמואל's own rule, so that case is ruled out. The only case left is a buyer from a גזלן, so שמואל seems to give that buyer שבח after all.

keyTerms.meaning: A creditor who takes land to collect his debt
The increase in the field's value
Produce or crops
Someone who bought land from a robber
'Rather, is it not...?' This forces the only remaining option.

phrases.english: In what case?
If it is about a creditor,
does he have rights to produce?
But didn't שמואל say:
A creditor collects the improvement,
meaning improvement, yes, but produce, no.
Rather, isn't it about one who buys from a robber!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָאו, בְּלוֹקֵחַ מִגַּזְלָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the קשיא from Step 11 by ruling out the creditor case.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's rule that a buyer from a גזלן gets no שבח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word פירי in the document cannot fit a בעל חוב, so the wording must protect a buyer from a גזלן, which means that buyer does get שבח.

steps.title: The case is where the robber owns land
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that the document wording is about a גזלן who owns land.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Here we are dealing with a case where he owns land.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף defends שמואל. He says the document wording is about a special case, where the seller (the גזלן) owns land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל's general rule, that a buyer from a גזלן gets no שבח, still stands. In the narrower case where the גזלן owns land, the payment for the improvement looks like part of a sale and not like extra payment on a loan, so it is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What are we dealing with here?' This introduces a narrower case.
Land
For example; as in a case where

phrases.english: רב יוסף said:
What are we dealing with here?
A case where he owns land.
phrases.notes: 'He' is the robber who sold the field.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Steps 11 and 12.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The document wording proves that every buyer from a גזלן gets שבח.
steps.terutzMaskana: The wording applies only where the גזלן owns land. Otherwise, שמואל's rule of no שבח still holds.

steps.title: Owning land doesn't help for borrowing a סאה for a סאה
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רב יוסף: owning land does not permit borrowing סאה בסאה, so why should it help here?
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Is it permitted to borrow a סאה for a סאה where he owns land?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רב יוסף's answer. He compares it to a known ריבית rule where owning land makes no difference.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים forbid borrowing a measure of grain and paying back the same measure, because the price might go up and it would look like ריבית. That rule applies even if the borrower owns land. So owning land should not make the robber's payment for the שבח acceptable either.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Is it really permitted?' A rhetorical challenge
To borrow
Borrowing a measure of grain to return the same measure later
Interest, which the Torah forbids

phrases.english: אביי said to him:
But is it permitted to borrow a סאה for a סאה
phrases.notes: A סאה is a measure of grain. He means borrowing a סאה now and paying back a סאה later.

phrases.english: in a case where he owns land?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי מוּתָּר לִלְוֹת סְאָה בִּסְאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יוסף's answer in Step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's claim that owning land makes the payment for שבח acceptable
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the case of סאה בסאה, owning land does not remove the problem of ריבית. So it should not remove it here either.

steps.title: A loan is different from a sale
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that סאה בסאה is a loan, while our case is a sale.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: There it is a loan; here it is a sale.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף explains why אביי's comparison does not work: a loan and a sale follow different rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With סאה בסאה, the extra value comes back on a loan, which is exactly what ריבית looks like, so owning land does not help. Here the buyer paid for a field, so it is a sale. Since the גזלן owns land, the extra he pays for the שבח does not look like interest.

keyTerms.meaning: A loan
A sale (Aramaic)
There / here. Used to contrast two cases.

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל: a buyer from a גזלן normally gets no שבח. רב יוסף limits this: if the גזלן owns land, the buyer may collect the שבח, because this deal is a sale. It is different from a loan like סאה בסאה, where owning land does not help.

phrases.english: He said to him:
There it is a loan,
here it is a sale.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם הַלְוָאָה, הָכָא זְבִינֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge in Step 14.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Owning land helps neither a loan nor a sale.
steps.terutzMaskana: Owning land matters for a sale, but not for a loan.

steps.title: Another version of רב יוסף's answer: a formal act of acquisition was made
steps.stepSummary: Some say רב יוסף answered differently: the document wording is about a case where a formal קנין was made with the seller.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say רב יוסף said: Here we are dealing with a case where they made a formal act of acquisition with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of רב יוסף's answer to the question on שמואל. In this version, the buyer made a formal קנין with the seller at the time of the sale.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version (step 13), רב יוסף said the case is about a גזלן who owns land. Here the answer is different: a קנין was made at the time of the sale, which locks in the seller's commitment to pay for improvements. Because the commitment is set from the start, the payment is not supposed to look like ריבית.

keyTerms.meaning: There are those who say (introduces another version of a statement)
Here, what case are we dealing with? (narrows the case)
They made a formal act of acquisition (קנין) with him, making his commitment binding

phrases.english: There are those who say:
Rav Yosef said:
Here, what are we dealing with?
A case where they made an act of acquisition with him.

steps.triggerLanguage: איכא דאמרי, אמר רב יוסף: הכא במאי עסקינן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of רב יוסף's answer from step 13, replacing 'a גזלן who owns land' with 'a case where a קנין was made'.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The document wording 'שופרא שבחא ופירי' seemed to show that a buyer from a גזלן collects שבח, which goes against שמואל.
steps.terutzMaskana: The wording is about a case where a formal קנין was made with the seller, so his commitment to pay for improvements was fixed from the start.

steps.title: אביי: a formal acquisition does not permit borrowing סאה בסאה
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks: making a קנין does not allow borrowing סאה בסאה, so why should it help here?
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: But is it permitted to borrow a סאה for a סאה in a case where they made a formal act of acquisition with him?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges this second version of רב יוסף's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Borrowing a סאה of grain and returning a סאה is forbidden, because the price might go up and the lender would get back more value. Making a קנין does not make that permitted. So אביי asks why a קנין should remove the ריבית problem in our case.

keyTerms.meaning: Borrowing a measure of produce and returning the same measure; forbidden because of ריבית
To borrow
In a case where

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
But is it permitted to borrow
a se'a for a se'a
phrases.notes: A סאה is a measure of grain. The borrower promises to return the same amount, even if its value goes up.

phrases.english: in a case where they made an act of acquisition with him?

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר ליה אביי: וכי מותר ללות סאה בסאה במקום שקנו מידו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer in step 16, the same way step 14 attacked step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's claim that a קנין removes the ריבית concern.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קנין does not permit סאה בסאה, so it should not permit collecting extra value here either.

steps.title: רב יוסף: that is a loan, this is a sale
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that סאה בסאה is a loan, but our case is a sale.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: There it is a loan, and here it is a sale.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers אביי by separating the two cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban of ריבית applies most strongly to loans, like borrowing סאה בסאה. Our case is a sale of land, so a payment for improvements that was agreed through a קנין is not counted as ריבית. This is the same answer as step 15, now given in the second version.

keyTerms.meaning: A loan
A sale (Aramaic)
There / here; a standard way of contrasting two cases

steps.whatToRemember: In both versions, רב יוסף's answers rest on one idea: a sale is treated differently from a loan when it comes to ריבית.

phrases.english: He said to him:
There it is a loan,
and here it is a sale.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר ליה: התם הלואה, והכא זביני
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge from step 17.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A קנין cannot permit ריבית, just as it does not permit סאה בסאה.
steps.terutzMaskana: סאה בסאה is a loan, where the ריבית ban applies. Our case is a sale, where it does not.

steps.title: Back to שמואל's statement: a creditor collects the improvement
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to שמואל's own statement: a בעל חוב collects the שבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now the statement itself: שמואל said: A creditor collects the improvement.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to discuss שמואל's own rule, which was quoted earlier in the sugya. This sets up רבא's proof in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: גופא means 'the matter itself': the גמרא returns to a statement it mentioned before and now discusses it directly. שמואל's rule is that when a בעל חוב takes land from a buyer, he also collects the value of the improvements made to it.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter itself; returning to a statement quoted earlier
A creditor
Collects
Improvement or increase in the land's value

phrases.english: The matter itself:
Shmuel said:
A creditor collects the improvement.

steps.triggerLanguage: גופא, אמר שמואל: בעל חוב גובה את השבח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the ריבית discussion and returns to שמואל's rule itself.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בעל חוב who takes land from a buyer also collects the value of its improvements.

steps.title: רבא proves שמואל's rule from the wording of a sale document
steps.stepSummary: רבא supports שמואל: the seller's standard guarantee in a sale document covers the land, the labor invested in it, and its improvements.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Know that this is true, for this is what a seller writes to the buyer: 'I will stand up and quiet, clear, and cleanse these sales, the land, the labor invested in it, and its improvements, and I will stand before you.' And this seller agreed and accepted it upon himself.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings a proof for שמואל from the standard wording a seller writes in a sale document.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the document, the seller guarantees to repay the buyer not just for the land, but also for the labor and the improvements. That guarantee only makes sense if the seller's בעל חוב can take the improvements from the buyer. So the standard document shows that a בעל חוב collects the שבח, just as שמואל said.

keyTerms.meaning: Know it; introduces a supporting proof
Seller / buyer
Their labor; the work invested in the land
I will cleanse; clear the land of any outside claims

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל's rule that a בעל חוב collects the שבח is backed by the seller's standard guarantee, which covers the improvements too.

phrases.english: Rava said: Know it,
for this is what the seller writes to the buyer:
"I will stand up and quiet
and clear and cleanse these sales,
phrases.notes: All these verbs mean the seller will deal with anyone who tries to take the land from the buyer.

phrases.english: them, and their labor, and their improvements,
and I will stand before you,
phrases.notes: He means he will make good and pay the buyer back.

phrases.english: and this seller agreed and accepted it upon himself."
phrases.notes: This last line is the witnesses' summary in the document, not the seller speaking.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רבא: תדע, שכך כותב לו מוכר ללוקח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports שמואל's rule from step 19.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's rule that a בעל חוב collects the שבח.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The standard wording of a sale document, in which the seller guarantees the land, the labor, and the improvements.

steps.title: What about a gift, which has no guarantee clause?
steps.stepSummary: רב חייא בר אבין challenges רבא: if the creditor takes the שבח only because of the sale document's wording, then a gift document without that wording would mean the creditor cannot take the שבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חייא בר אבין said to רבא: If so, a gift document does not have this wording. Would you really say the creditor does not take the improvements from the person who got the gift?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב חייא בר אבין attacks רבא's proof by pointing to a case where the special wording is missing: a gift.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא based the creditor's right to the שבח on the seller's written guarantee, which covers land, labor and improvements. A gift document does not include that guarantee. Following רבא's logic, the creditor would not take the שבח from a gift recipient, and that result sounds strange.

keyTerms.meaning: "But if so": the reasoning is being pushed to see where it leads
A gift
Takes away, repossesses (a creditor seizing land)
The improvement or increase in the land's value

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָבִין לְרָבָא:
phrases.english: Rav Chiyya bar Avin said to Rava:
But if that is so,
a gift, where he does not write this for him,
phrases.notes: "This" means the guarantee wording from step 20: land, labor and improvements.

phrases.english: would you really say that the creditor does not take the improvement?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה מַתָּנָה דְּלָא כָּתֵיב לֵיהּ הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's proof from step 20 by pointing to its consequence for a gift
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's proof that the creditor collects שבח because of the sale document's guarantee clause
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the clause is the reason, then a gift without the clause should leave the שבח with the recipient, and that seems unacceptable

steps.title: רבא accepts: yes, no improvements from a gift
steps.stepSummary: רבא accepts the result: the creditor indeed does not take the שבח from a gift recipient.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: Yes.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא does not back down. He agrees that with a gift, the creditor does not take the improvements.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of defending his proof by finding a difference, רבא simply accepts the conclusion. The guarantee clause is exactly what lets the creditor take the שבח. Where there is no clause, as with a gift, the creditor does not get the שבח.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes
The person who receives a gift
The creditor

phrases.english: He said to him: Yes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 21 by accepting its result
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed impossible that a gift recipient would keep the שבח
steps.terutzMaskana: He does keep it. The creditor takes the שבח only where a sale's guarantee clause exists

steps.title: Is a gift really stronger than a sale?
steps.stepSummary: רב חייא בר אבין presses again: does it make sense that a gift gives the recipient a stronger hold than a sale gives a buyer?
steps.simpleTranslation: But is the power of a gift stronger than the power of a sale?
steps.whatsHappening: רב חייא בר אבין points out how odd רבא's answer sounds: a gift recipient would be better protected than a paying buyer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A buyer paid money, while a gift recipient paid nothing. Normally we would expect the buyer to have the stronger claim. Under רבא's answer, though, the buyer loses the שבח to the creditor and the gift recipient keeps it.

keyTerms.meaning: "But is it really...?": a surprised question
Has stronger legal power
A sale

phrases.english: But is the power of a gift stronger than that of a sale?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי יָפֶה כֹּחַ מַתָּנָה מִמֶּכֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes back against רבא's acceptance in step 22
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that the creditor does not take the שבח from a gift recipient
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It is unreasonable for a free gift to give a stronger right than a paid sale

steps.title: רבא: yes, a gift is indeed stronger here
steps.stepSummary: רבא insists that in this respect a gift really is stronger than a sale.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: Yes, it is indeed stronger.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא stands firm and says that here a gift truly does give more protection than a sale.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A seller promises the buyer to cover land, labor and improvements, and that promise is what lets the creditor reach the שבח. A giver makes no such promise, so the creditor cannot take the שבח from the recipient. The odd-sounding result follows directly from how the documents are written.

keyTerms.meaning: "Stronger, and indeed stronger": a strong yes
A buyer
The seller's guarantee to pay back the buyer if the land is taken

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, a creditor takes the שבח from a buyer, because the sale document's guarantee covers improvements. He does not take it from a gift recipient. So in this specific respect, a gift is stronger than a sale.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean a gift is stronger than a sale in general. רבא is talking only about whether the creditor can take the improvements.

phrases.english: He said to him: Yes, it is indeed stronger.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 23 by firmly accepting its result
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A sale should always give at least as much power as a gift
steps.terutzMaskana: Regarding שבח, a gift is stronger, because it has no guarantee clause for the creditor to rely on

steps.title: רב נחמן brings a ברייתא that supports שמואל
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן says a ברייתא supports שמואל, while noting that רב הונא explains it differently. In the ברייתא, a buyer whose field was taken collects the principal from sold property and the improvement from free property.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: This ברייתא supports שמואל, but our colleague הונא explains it as talking about other matters. It is taught: If someone sells a field to another, and it is taken away from the buyer, then when the buyer collects from the seller, he collects the principal even from property the seller later sold, and he collects the improvement only from property the seller still owns.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן offers a new proof for שמואל from a ברייתא. Right away he warns that רב הונא reads it in a way that removes the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, the buyer gets back the value of the improvements from his seller. That means the buyer lost those improvements when the field was taken. This fits שמואל: the creditor took the field together with its שבח.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא, a teaching of the תנאים outside the משנה
Supports
Explains it as talking about a specific case
The principal: the basic price of the field
Property the seller has since sold to others, which is still tied to his debt
Free property the seller still owns

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:

phrases.aramaic: הָא מַתְנִיתָא מְסַיַּיע לֵיהּ לְמָר שְׁמוּאֵל,
phrases.english: This ברייתא supports Mar Shmuel,

phrases.aramaic: וְהוּנָא חַבְרִין מוֹקֵים לַהּ בְּמִילֵּי אַחֲרִינֵי.
phrases.english: but our colleague Huna explains it as being about other matters.
As it is taught: One who sells a field to another,
and it is then taken out of the buyer's possession,
when the buyer collects, he collects the principal
from liened property,
phrases.notes: He means land the seller sold to other people after this sale. That land is still tied to the seller's obligation.

phrases.english: and he collects the improvement from free property.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא מַתְנִיתָא מְסַיַּיע לֵיהּ לְמָר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a second support for שמואל's rule from step 19, after רבא's proof
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's rule that a creditor collects the שבח
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: a buyer whose field was taken collects the שבח from the seller's free property, which shows the שבח was taken from him

steps.title: רב הונא: the ברייתא is about buying from a robber
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא explains the ברייתא as talking about someone who bought a field from a גזלן, so it does not prove anything about a creditor.
steps.simpleTranslation: But our colleague הונא explains it as talking about other matters: someone who bought from a robber.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains the other reading that רב נחמן mentioned. רב הונא says the field in the ברייתא was taken back by its real owner from a robber, not by a creditor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the seller was a גזלן, the true owner takes back his own field together with everything that grew or improved on it. That is why the buyer lost the שבח. It does not show that a creditor collects the שבח, so the proof for שמואל falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: Our colleague
Other matters, a different case
A robber
Someone who bought from a robber

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the ברייתא can be read two ways. So it cannot settle whether a creditor takes the שבח.

phrases.english: But our colleague Huna explains it
phrases.notes: The גמרא repeats רב נחמן's words from step 25 to spell out how רב הונא reads it.

phrases.english: as being about other matters: one who buys from a robber.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהוּנָא חַבְרִין מוֹקֵים לַהּ בְּמִילֵּי אַחֲרִינֵי בְּלוֹקֵחַ מִגַּזְלָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains רב הונא's reading, which was mentioned in step 25, and removes the proof
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the ברייתא as a proof for שמואל, without rejecting שמואל's rule itself
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא may be about a field taken back by the victim of a robbery, not about a creditor collecting a debt

steps.title: Another ברייתא: who pays the buyer for his improvement
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules on a buyer who improved a field that a creditor then seized. If the שבח is more than the expenses, the buyer gets the extra שבח from the seller and his expenses from the creditor. If the expenses are more, he gets his expenses from the creditor, but only up to the value of the שבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא teaches: Someone sold a field, the buyer improved it, and then a creditor came and seized it. When the buyer collects, there are two cases. If the improvement is worth more than what he spent, he takes the improvement from the seller and his expenses from the creditor. If what he spent is more than the improvement, he only gets his expenses from the creditor, up to the value of the improvement.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא that deals with a buyer, an improvement, and a creditor. This step only lays out the source; the next step will ask how שמואל fits with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא splits the buyer's payback into two parts: expenses and the extra value beyond the expenses. The creditor pays for the expenses (up to the שבח), and the seller pays for the extra שבח. So the creditor does not get the improvement for free, which seems to clash with שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: It is taught in another ברייתא
The rise in the field's value from the buyer's work
The money the buyer spent to improve the field
He seized it (a creditor taking sold land to collect a debt)
Owner of the land. Here it means the seller.

steps.confusionAlert: "בַּעַל הַקַּרְקַע" here is the seller who sold the field, not the creditor who seized it.

phrases.english: It is taught in another ברייתא:
One who sells a field to his fellow, and the buyer improved it,
and a creditor came and seized it,
when the buyer collects,
if the improvement is more than the expenses,
he takes the improvement from the owner of the land,
phrases.notes: He gets the extra value beyond what he spent from the seller, who sold him the field.

phrases.english: and the expenses from the creditor.
And if the expenses are more than the improvement,
he has only his expenses,
up to the amount of the improvement, from the creditor.

steps.triggerLanguage: תניא אידך
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רב הונא pushed off the first ברייתא, the גמרא brings a second ברייתא on the same topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A buyer whose improved field is seized by a creditor gets his expenses (up to the שבח) from the creditor, and any extra שבח from the seller.

steps.title: Neither reading of the ברייתא fits שמואל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how שמואל can explain the ברייתא. If it is about a buyer from a גזלן, the first part clashes with שמואל, because he holds such a buyer gets no שבח. If it is about a creditor, both parts clash with שמואל, because he holds a creditor collects the שבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: How does שמואל explain this ברייתא? If it is about someone who bought from a robber, the first part is a problem, because שמואל said a buyer from a robber gets no improvement. If it is about a creditor, the first and last parts are both problems, because שמואל said a creditor collects the improvement.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges שמואל: the ברייתא does not seem to fit his view under either possible reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא could be read as a case of a robber (like רב הונא read the earlier ברייתא) or as a case of a real creditor. In the robber reading, the רישא gives the buyer שבח, against שמואל. In the creditor reading, both the רישא and the סיפא make the creditor pay for expenses, while שמואל says the creditor simply takes the שבח.

keyTerms.meaning: Sets it up; explains which case the source is talking about
One who bought a field from a robber
The first part of the source
The last part of the source

phrases.english: But how does שמואל set up this ברייתא?
If it is about one who bought from a robber,
the first part is difficult,
phrases.notes: The first part gives the buyer the improvement. That is exactly what שמואל says a robber's buyer doesn't get.

phrases.english: since שמואל said:
One who buys from a robber does not get the improvement.
If it is about a creditor,
the first part and the last part are difficult,
since שמואל said:
A creditor collects the improvement!

steps.triggerLanguage: והא שמואל במאי מוקים לה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ברייתא just quoted to attack שמואל.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's two rulings: a buyer from a גזלן gets no שבח, and a creditor collects the שבח.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both possible readings of the ברייתא give the buyer payment that שמואל would deny him.

steps.title: First answer: a robber who owns land, or a קנין was made
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is about a buyer from a גזלן, but in a special case. Either the robber owns land, or the buyer made a קנין from the robber at the time of the sale. In such a case even שמואל agrees the buyer gets the שבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say it is about one who bought from a robber, where the robber has land. Or else, where they made a קנין from his hand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for שמואל by reading the ברייתא as a robber case. It limits the case to special situations where the buyer may collect the שבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל's rule that a robber's buyer gets no שבח is a general rule, and here it has an exception. If the robber owns land, he pays with land rather than money, so the payment does not look like interest. Or, if a קנין was made at the sale, the buyer already acquired his right to the שבח back then. Either way, the רישא no longer clashes with שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say; it introduces one possible answer
Or else; another possibility
They made a formal act of acquisition (קנין) from him

phrases.english: If you want, say it is about one who bought from a robber,
for example, where he has land.
phrases.notes: "He" is the robber, who has land he can pay the buyer with.

phrases.english: Or else, where they made a קנין from his hand.

steps.triggerLanguage: איבעית אימא בלוקח מגזלן כגון שיש לו קרקע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא by choosing the robber reading and narrowing it to a special case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא) to an exception
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A robber case would always clash with שמואל's rule that such a buyer gets no שבח.
steps.terutzMaskana: When the robber owns land, or a קנין was made, even שמואל lets the buyer collect the שבח.

steps.title: Second answer begins: it is about a creditor after all
steps.stepSummary: A second answer keeps the ברייתא about a real creditor and says there is no clash with שמואל. The גמרא starts a distinction with "here it is talking about שבח...", and that distinction continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say it is about a creditor, and it is still not difficult: here it is talking about an improvement...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a second way to defend שמואל, reading the ברייתא as a creditor case. It starts to tell two kinds of improvement apart, and the rest of the line comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the גמרא does not move the case to a robber. It plans to show that the ברייתא and שמואל are talking about different kinds of שבח. The words "כאן בשבח" open that contrast; the full distinction is finished in the next lines.

keyTerms.meaning: And it is not difficult; the two sources can both stand
Here; points to one side of a contrast between two cases

phrases.english: If you want, say it is about a creditor.
And it is not difficult:
here it is talking about an improvement

steps.triggerLanguage: איבעית אימא בבעל חוב ולא קשיא כאן בשבח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, different answer to the same קשיא, this time keeping the creditor reading.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing between two kinds of שבח (כאן / כאן)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A creditor reading would clash with שמואל on both the רישא and the סיפא.
steps.terutzMaskana: Not yet complete here: the ברייתא and שמואל will be shown to talk about different kinds of שבח.
